support.quote: What used to be East Berlin still utilizes nearly 40,000 sodium-vapour lamps, which appear orange, while what used to be West Berlin has upgraded to mercury vapour, fluorescent or LED lamps that appear white.
Seen from above, street lights in the former East Berlin appear slightly more orange while those in the western part of the city are a harsher yellow.

assessments.note: 2019; a city spokesman attributes the difference more to fittings and shades than to lamp types.

support.quote: Seen from space, the city's lights show a stark contrast, with orange lights in the east and white lights in the west.
Over the last two decades astronauts are witnessing from space how cities shine whiter at night as new street lighting technologies were introduced.

assessments.note: 2022 ISS images (2012 vs 2022) show Berlin's lighting changing (whitening); supports that the contrast is fading — time-sensitive.
